<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Support `return_token_offsets` on Rust completion and chat render endpoints, covering the item in #44280. Responses include per-token character spans from the supplied completion prompt or templated chat prompt.

Fastokens has no offset API. Keep its token IDs and return spans from a lazily cached HF tokenizer only when the complete ID sequences match. Default requests still encode once; opting in retains another tokenizer and encodes twice.

## Claims

- Return Unicode character spans aligned with token IDs, including after truncation. Chat spans refer to the templated prompt.
- Preserve token IDs; return `null` when offsets are not requested or unavailable.

## Validation

Rebased onto `2d69083c4` on October 9. Rust 1.95, macOS arm64: **99 tokenizer tests passed**, along with tokenizer clippy, formatting, and applicable pre-commit hooks. The rebase preserves upstream reasoning controls; the existing render-to-generate test checks these together with offsets.

Full-workspace compilation currently fails at `socket2::Socket::domain` in `engine-core-client/src/transport.rs:408`. The same failure reproduces on unchanged main (`2d69083c4`), introduced by #54113. Linux validation is still needed; the local Docker image pull failed with a container metadata I/O error.

Before this rebase, **2,016 Rust tests**, 13 Qwen HTTP reference cases, and 31 long-prompt/concurrency checks passed, as did full-workspace clippy, the CLI build, and the strict docs build. These are prior-revision results, not a full pass for the rebased commit.

Hosted CI still requires maintainer authorization. No GPU inference or model-quality evaluation is claimed: this change concerns engine-free preprocessing and preserves token IDs.

<details>
<summary>Commands and coverage</summary>

Run from the repository root with the pinned Rust toolchain and `PYO3_PYTHON` pointing to the checkout's Python environment:

```bash
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p vllm-tokenizer --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p vllm-tokenizer --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --run-ignored only --test-threads 1
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check
cargo build --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p vllm-cmd --all-features --locked
git diff --name-only -z HEAD^ HEAD | xargs -0 .venv/bin/pre-commit run --hook-stage manual --files
```

Before the rebase, the normal workspace run passed 2,003 tests; all 13 normally ignored tests passed separately. Key regressions cover source-character offsets and unchanged IDs, companion-tokenizer disagreement, and truncation across repeated preparation. Existing Rust Buildkite jobs cover these files.

HTTP checks compare exact IDs/spans with HF tokenizers and the official chat template, including Unicode, default/false/null flags, left/right truncation, and pre-tokenized input. The model revision is `c1899de289a04d12100db370d81485cdf75e47ca`. In-tree HTTP tests use HF; tokenizer tests cover both backends. The docs build used `mkdocs build --strict` with pinned docs requirements.

The initial full run hit a Gemma download-lock failure and a grammar-replay timeout. The Gemma rerun, direct grammar helper, and complete workspace rerun passed without changing tests or timeouts. An earlier audio timing failure also reproduced on the unchanged base.

</details>

## Details

With Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B, this request to `/v1/completions/render`:

```json
{"model":"Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B","prompt":"café 🙂","max_tokens":8,"add_special_tokens":false,"return_token_offsets":true}
```

returns these fields in its first result:

```json
{"token_ids":[924,58858,27484],"token_offsets":[[0,2],[2,4],[4,6]]}
```

Companion initialization runs on a blocking worker; encoding remains synchronous. Long opted-in requests can delay other requests on constrained workers.

<details>
<summary>Local performance diagnostic</summary>

A single two-worker debug run used 16,384-token Qwen prompts. Warm offset requests took 54–55 ms versus 7–9 ms without offsets; first-use initialization and encoding took about 1.04 s. Observed RSS rose about 120 MiB, including allocator retention and caches. A health request overlapping four long offset requests took 98 ms. All 31 reference checks passed.

These measurements describe opt-in costs; they are not a production throughput benchmark.

</details>

Chat responses do not include the rendered prompt text or a mapping back to individual messages. Rendered responses remain accepted by `/generate`, which ignores this metadata. Consuming `token_offsets` and preprocessed multimodal features in `/generate` remains a separate roadmap item. Searches of #44280 activity and related PRs found no competing Rust offset implementation.

---

<details>
<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

**BEFORE SUBMITTING, PLEASE READ <https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/contributing>** (anything written below this line will be removed by GitHub Actions)

@@ -26,6 +26,17 @@ vllm serve <model> --enable-scale-out
 - [Responses Render API](renderer.md) (`/v1/responses/render`)
     - Render a self-contained Responses request
 
+## Rust renderer token offsets
+
+For `vllm-rs render`, set `return_token_offsets: true` on completion or chat
+render requests to include per-token `[start, end]` spans in `token_offsets`.
+Spans count Unicode code points; chat spans refer to the templated prompt.
+Truncation preserves the original coordinates. The field is `null` when not requested,
+for pre-tokenized prompts, or when the tokenizer cannot supply matching offsets.
+The Rust render server rejects multimodal requests.
+Fastokens uses an additional cached HF tokenizer for this
+opt-in path, adding memory usage and a second encoding.
+
 ## Get Responses prompt token IDs
 
 Use `/v1/responses/render` to get prompt token IDs before choosing a model

@@ -122,6 +122,16 @@ It exposes `/v1/chat/completions/render` and `/v1/completions/render`. Only
 tokenizer and model configuration files are loaded; model weights, PyTorch,
 and vLLM kernels are not required.
 
+Set `return_token_offsets: true` to include per-token `[start, end]` character
+spans (Unicode code points) in `token_offsets`. Chat spans refer to the prompt
+after applying the chat template; truncation retains coordinates in that original
+prompt. Pre-tokenized prompts and unsupported tokenizers return `null`.
+Multimodal requests are rejected by this text-only server.
+Spans follow Hugging Face semantics: they can overlap, and inserted
+special tokens have span `[0, 0]`. With Fastokens, offsets use a lazily loaded
+Hugging Face tokenizer only when its token IDs match exactly. This opt-in path
+tokenizes twice and retains an additional tokenizer in memory.
+
 To serve HTTPS, pass `--ssl-certfile`. If the certificate and private key are
 in separate files, pass `--ssl-keyfile` for the key; otherwise the key is read from
 the certificate file. For mTLS, pass `--ssl-ca-certs` with a CA
